cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A sequence of operations is analyzed by assigning a global potential to states and proving that each local operation can change the accounted quantity only by a bounded amount.
common_abstraction: global quantity accumulated through a sequence of local operations
local change budget implies a lower bound on the number of costly operations needed to reach a high-potential state

costly local operation -> counted binary intersection/fusion
terminal stored potential -> target graph/set-family invariant value

cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Search first for a union-free, cyclic-reuse-safe potential with bounded one-intersection increase; only then ask whether any explicit target has super-logarithmic potential.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For any proposed potential, prove zero or absorbable change under free union, prove a uniform bound under one legal intersection in the exact cyclic semantics, and run C010-C023 compression families as counterexamples before target evaluation.
